transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Ross (Redwood); Priya Kapoor, Daniel Brooks, Laura Chen, Samir Iqbal (Aurora)

SUMMARY:
Maya: quick scoping to align on workload, QPS, concurrency, token distribution, and POC success criteria. We'll run a 4-6 week pilot with focused benchmarks (latency p95, quality/regression, and cost).

TOPICS COVERED:
- Current infra / stack and authentication
- Traffic modeling: peak QPS, sustained QPS, concurrency, burst tolerance
- Token distributions (input / output averages and tail cases)
- Benchmarks: models to test, quantization, dedicated vs hosted, dataset for eval
- Success criteria & go/no-go metrics

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we've got most folks. quick intros and then Ethan will walk through the benchmark template.
[00:08] Priya: hi i'm priya, head of ml at aurora, i'm leading the POC.
[00:11] Daniel: daniel, platform eng, i'll be owning the infra side.
[00:14] Laura: laura, product, prioritizing the success metrics.
[00:16] Samir: samir from security, i'll flag any compliance items.
[00:19] Ethan: awesome thanks, so goal for today is to agree on workload numbers — QPS, concurrency, token distributions — and make sure the POC scope maps to your success criteria.
[00:29] Laura: high level: we want an assistant that does KYC support and payment routing suggestions, so responses are usually short but occasionally long with receipts and logs. target latency needs to be under 200ms p95 ideally 150ms for UI snappiness.
[00:46] Priya: current qps in prod is about 18 qps sustained, peak bursts up to 60 qps during morning batch windows. concurrency wise we see ~12 concurrent sessions normally, spikes to 40 for heavy users.
[01:02] Daniel: we run on gke on GCP, use cloud sql and a redis kv for caching. we try to keep the kv cache warm for prefixes.
[01:12] Maya: cool that's helpful. for modeling we usually ask for three numbers: sustained qps, burst qps, and concurrency. so from what i'm hearing: sustained 18 qps, peak 60 qps, concurrency 12-40. does that match?
[01:23] Priya: yes that matches. also note token distribution: 60% of requests <50 input tokens, 35% between 50-512, 5% long >512. outputs are typically 20-120 tokens, with a very small tail for long transcripts (~1% > 2000 tokens) when we return logs.
[01:41] Ethan: that's great detail. for the POC we recommend sampling 5k prompts that reflect that distribution and add 200 long-tail prompts to stress KV / attention.
[01:51] Samir: on security, we need SOC 2 attestation, SAML SSO, KMS for key management, and audit logs kept for 12 months. any additional network controls for Private?
[02:03] Maya: yes we'll include our security pack; Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC and HSM/KMS integration. we'll attach the SOC 2 and SAML integration doc.
[02:12] Laura: cost target is important — stakeholder wants cost per inference lower than our current vendor. ballpark we want under $0.0006 per token all-in, otherwise it gets harder to justify.
[02:24] Ethan: we can tune with batching and quantization to get costs down. for initial runs we'll test the open models (e.g., Llama-2 variants) and Redwood-verified configs. suggest model matrix: Llama2-13b int8, Llama2-70b q4, and a gated production model if needed.
[02:38] Priya: side question: do you support streaming and function/tool calling for structured outputs? we definitely need streaming for the UI.
[02:45] Maya: yes streaming is supported; function calling is supported as well though we should validate schema mapping in the POC tests.
[02:51] Daniel: about latency SLO: given your batching and KV cache does the p95 include queuing? we really care about tail for interactive UI.
[02:59] Ethan: p95 includes end-to-end server response time. queuing can be tuned with concurrency and autoscaling in Dedicated. For the POC we'll measure cold vs warm KV cache, and look at p50/p90/p95.
[03:12] Priya: what about throughput? to get 60 qps peaks we may need dedicated capacity or host with burst policies.
[03:19] Maya: correct — options are hosted with burst (may have cold starts) or Redwood Dedicated reserved pools for steady throughput. we can model both: run benchmarks on a Dedicated-like instance and a hosted bucket to compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:31] Laura: timeline — we want pilot results in ~4 weeks with a decision at 6 weeks. is that feasible?
[03:37] Maya: yes typical POC is 4-6 weeks: week 1 ingest datasets and baseline, week 2 run baseline benchmarks, week 3 iterate on quant/serve config, week 4 execute long-tail tests and produce report. optionally weeks 5-6 if integration/SSO or Private infra needs more time.
[03:50] Ethan: i'll add the exact test matrix: qps ramps (sustained 18 qps for 30m, burst to 60 qps for 5m, concurrency sweep from 4 to 40), token-size buckets, cold vs warm cache, and model variants.
[04:03] Samir: what data retention / logs will you share? we can't share PII in training.
[04:09] Maya: we don't use customer data to train models. for the benchmark we'll operate on hashed or synthetic prompts; logs retained for troubleshooting and can be configured to mask PII.
[04:17] Priya: ok can you run a quick back-of-envelope for required GPU capacity assuming Llama2-70b q4 and our distribution?
[04:23] Ethan: rough calc: if avg request is 200 tokens (input+output), and an optimized 70b q4 run gives ~8 tok/ms on an A100-class node under our runtime — very rough — for 18 qps sustained that's ~144 tok/ms aggregate, which maps to X nodes; let me be clear i'm simplifying, we'll run proper perf tests.
[04:41] Daniel: can we schedule a 2-hour spike test where we push to 60 qps and observe autoscaling? we control the client side.
[04:48] Ethan: yes we'll provide a harness and runbook. prefer to coordinate exact time so we don't hit production.
[04:54] Laura: success criteria recap: p95 latency <150ms for median cases, no regressions on quality >3% compared to current model, cost per token < $0.0006, SSO + KMS integrations validated.
[05:07] Maya: agreed. we'll put those into the POC doc as go/no-go gates.
[05:11] Priya: for quality regression how do you measure? we'll provide golden responses and accuracy metric?
[05:16] Ethan: we usually run exact match / BLEU-like metrics for structured outputs and human eval for generative quality on a sample. also track hallucination rate on a labeled set.
[05:26] Priya: ok we'll prepare a labeled set of 500 golden prompts.
[05:29] Maya: perfect. next steps — i'll send the benchmark template and the security pack, ethan will schedule the load test and share the harness.
[05:36] Daniel: thanks — do you have pricing bands for Dedicated vs Hosted for this scale?
[05:40] Maya: yes i'll include estimated pricing for a 3-month reserved vs on-demand hosted; we'll show per-token and per-hour GPU costs.
[05:47] Samir: please also include audit log retention and support SLAs.
[05:50] Maya: noted.
[05:52] Laura: any open blockers?
[05:55] Priya: none from my side — just need the sample dataset and timeline.
[05:58] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with docs and schedule.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
